name: New Wave

influenced_by: punk's DIY energy, redirected through art-school irony

media.title: Devo's matching jumpsuits and energy-dome hats (late 1970s on)

reacts_against: punk's raw aggression, keeping its DIY, anti-corporate spirit but channeling it through synthesizers, art-school concept and a more deliberately stylized visual presentation.
revivals: directly cited by synthwave's 1980s-referencing visual language
article: New wave grew out of the same late-1970s scene that produced punk, sharing its DIY, anti-corporate-rock attitude but trading raw guitar aggression for synthesizers, angular art-school concept and a far more deliberate visual sensibility. Bands like Talking Heads and Devo treated the stage presentation itself as part of the art — Devo performed in matching industrial jumpsuits and red "energy dome" hats, a costume as conceptually loaded as their music. The genre's rise coincided almost exactly with MTV's 1981 launch, and new wave's sharper, more graphic visual style (bold color-blocking, geometric shapes, structured tailoring) was unusually well suited to the new medium, which helped push it toward mainstream pop success faster than punk itself ever achieved. That synthesizer-and-geometry visual language became a direct ancestor of 1980s-nostalgic genres decades later, most clearly synthwave, which revives new wave and its adjacent synth-pop scene's color and font choices almost wholesale.
